title: Registr: rasmiydan so‘zlashuvgacha
goal_uz: Dars oxirida bitta fikrni beshta registrda (rasmiy, neytral, norasmiy, so‘zlashuv, sleng) ifodalaysiz, Britaniya va Amerika so‘zlashuv so‘zlarini tanib olasiz, vaziyatga qarab registrni almashtirasiz va yozma hamda og‘zaki nutq farqini qo‘llaysiz.

scenes.title: Bugun: registr
board: Register: from formal to colloquial
(Registr: rasmiydan so‘zlashuvgacha)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda C2 darajasi nimani anglatishini ko‘rib, shaxsiy rejangizni tuzdingiz. Bugun C2 ning eng muhim belgilaridan biri, registrni o‘rganamiz. Dars oxirida bitta fikrni bir necha uslubda ayta olasiz, so‘zlashuv va slengni tanib olasiz va qachon qaysi uslubga o‘tishni bilasiz.
scenes.say: Knowing what to say is only half the job. The other half is knowing how to say it, to this person, in this situation.
scenes.say_uz: Nima deyishni bilish ishning yarmi. Qolgan yarmi buni shu odamga, shu vaziyatda qanday aytishni bilish.

scenes.title: Registr nima?
board: Register = level of formality
Depends on: audience · purpose · channel · relationship
scenes.say_native: Registr nutqning rasmiylik darajasi. U to‘rt narsaga bog‘liq: kimga gapiryapsiz, nima maqsadda, qaysi kanal orqali, ya’ni xatmi, telefonmi, yuzma-yuzmi, va o‘rtangizdagi munosabat qanday. Grammatik jihatdan to‘g‘ri gap noto‘g‘ri registrda aytilsa, xuddi to‘yga sport kiyimida kelgandek bo‘ladi: xato emas, lekin o‘rinsiz.
scenes.say: Register is the level of formality you choose. It depends on who you're talking to, why, through which channel, and how well you know them.
scenes.say_uz: Registr siz tanlagan rasmiylik darajasi. U kimga gapirayotganingiz, nima uchun, qaysi kanal orqali va uni qanchalik yaxshi bilishingizga bog‘liq.

scenes.title: Registr shkalasi
board: Formal: We regret to inform you that your application has been unsuccessful.
Neutral: Unfortunately, your application was not successful.
Informal: I'm afraid you didn't get the job.
Colloquial/slang: Sorry, mate, no luck this time.
scenes.say_native: Shkalani besh pog‘ona deb tasavvur qiling: rasmiy, neytral, norasmiy, so‘zlashuv va sleng. Doskadagi to‘rt gap bitta xabarni beradi: ishga olinmadingiz. Rasmiy gapda majhul nisbat va “we regret to inform you” bor, norasmiyda “I’m afraid”, eng pastda esa “mate” va qisqa ibora. Neytral registr eng xavfsiz: uni deyarli har qanday vaziyatda ishlatish mumkin.
scenes.say: We regret to inform you that your application has been unsuccessful. I'm afraid you didn't get the job. Sorry, mate, no luck this time. Same news, three very different relationships.
scenes.say_uz: Afsus bilan ma’lum qilamizki, arizangiz muvaffaqiyatsiz bo‘ldi. Afsuski, ishga olinmadingiz. Kechir, do‘stim, bu safar omad kulmadi. Bitta xabar, uchta butunlay boshqa munosabat.

scenes.title: So‘rov shkalasi
board: Would you be so kind as to close the window?
Could you close the window, please?
Can you close the window?
Shut the window, will you?

examples.t: I was wondering if you could help me.
examples.uz: Menga yordam bera olarmikansiz deb o‘ylagandim. (juda muloyim)

scenes.say_native: So‘rovlarda shkala ayniqsa yaqqol. “Would you be so kind as to…” juda rasmiy, hatto biroz eskicha. “Could you…, please?” neytral va xavfsiz. “Can you…?” do‘stona. “Shut the window, will you?” esa yaqin odamlar orasida. Muloyimlikni o‘tgan zamon ham oshiradi: “I was wondering if…” hozirgi zamondagi “I wonder” dan yumshoqroq eshitiladi.
scenes.say: Would you be so kind as to close the window? Could you close the window, please? Can you close the window? Shut the window, will you? Each step down the ladder assumes a closer relationship.
scenes.say_uz: Derazani yopib qo‘yish iltifotini qilmaysizmi? Derazani yopib bera olasizmi? Derazani yopasanmi? Derazani yop-chi. Har bir pastki pog‘ona yaqinroq munosabatni nazarda tutadi.

scenes.title: Rasmiylik belgilari
board: Formal: Latinate verbs · passive · nominalisation · Should you require…
Informal: phrasal verbs · contractions · short sentences
Colloquial: ellipsis · vague language · tags

examples.t: Should you require further assistance, please contact us.
examples.uz: Qo‘shimcha yordam kerak bo‘lsa, biz bilan bog‘laning. (rasmiy inversiya)

scenes.say_native: Registrni qanday tanish mumkin? Rasmiy uslubda lotincha fe’llar, majhul nisbat, otlashtirish va “Should you require…” kabi inversiya ko‘p. Norasmiy uslubda ibora fe’llar va “don’t”, “I’ll” kabi qisqartmalar ustun. So‘zlashuvda esa gaplar tushib qoladi: “Want a coffee?”, noaniq iboralar paydo bo‘ladi: “and stuff”, “sort of”. Bu belgilarni bilsangiz, matnni bir qarashda baholaysiz.
scenes.say: Formal English favours Latinate verbs, the passive and structures like should you require. Informal English prefers phrasal verbs and contractions. Colloquial speech drops words altogether: want a coffee?
scenes.say_uz: Rasmiy ingliz tili lotincha fe’llar, majhul nisbat va should you require kabi tuzilmalarni afzal ko‘radi. Norasmiy til ibora fe’l va qisqartmalarni yoqtiradi. So‘zlashuvda esa so‘zlar butunlay tushib qoladi: kofe ichasanmi?

scenes.title: O‘zbek tili bilan solishtirish
board: Uzbek: sen / siz / Siz · -lar (hurmat)
English: only 'you' → register through words and grammar
tashrif buyurmoq ≈ attend · kelmoq ≈ come
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida registr ko‘p hollarda “sen” va “siz” orqali, hurmat ma’nosidagi “-lar” orqali bildiriladi: “dadam keldilar”. Ingliz tilida esa faqat “you” bor, shuning uchun hurmat so‘z tanlash va grammatika orqali beriladi. Lekin o‘xshashlik ham bor: o‘zbekchada arab-fors so‘zlari rasmiyroq, “tashrif buyurmoq” va “kelmoq”. Inglizchada ham lotincha “attend” rasmiy, oddiy “come” esa kundalik.
scenes.say: English has only one word for you, so politeness has to come from vocabulary and grammar: could instead of can, attend instead of come, and a softening phrase like I'm afraid.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida “siz” uchun bitta so‘z bor, shuning uchun muloyimlik so‘z va grammatikadan keladi: can o‘rniga could, come o‘rniga attend va I’m afraid kabi yumshatuvchi ibora.

scenes.title: Registr nomuvofiqligi
board: ✗ Dear Sir or Madam, I wanna complain about my order.
✓ Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to complain about my order.
✗ (to a friend) I shall endeavour to procure some beverages.
✓ I'll grab some drinks.
scenes.say_native: Nomuvofiqlik ikki tomonga bo‘ladi. Rasmiy xatda “wanna” ishlatsangiz, xatingiz jiddiy qabul qilinmaydi. Do‘stingizga “I shall endeavour to procure some beverages” desangiz, u kulib yuboradi, chunki bu “ichimlik olib kelaman” ning saroy tilidagi varianti. C1 o‘quvchilari ko‘pincha ikkinchi xatoni qiladi: kitobdan o‘rgangan rasmiy so‘zni hamma joyda ishlatadi.
scenes.say: Mismatches work both ways. Wanna in a complaint letter sounds careless. I shall endeavour to procure some beverages, said to a friend, sounds like a butler in a comedy. Just say: I'll grab some drinks.
scenes.say_uz: Nomuvofiqlik ikki tomonlama. Shikoyat xatidagi wanna beparvo eshitiladi. Do‘stga aytilgan I shall endeavour to procure some beverages esa komediyadagi xizmatkorga o‘xshaydi. Shunchaki I’ll grab some drinks deng.

scenes.title: Mashq: rasmiydan so‘zlashuvga tartiblang
board: a) Gimme a sec.
b) Could you wait a moment, please?
c) Hang on a minute.
d) Kindly wait while we process your request.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap bir xil ma’noni beradi: kutib turing. Ularni eng rasmiysidan eng so‘zlashuvga qarab tartiblang. Har biri qayerda eshitilishi mumkinligini ham o‘ylang: bank saytida, do‘konda, do‘stlar orasida. Javobni harflar bilan yozing, masalan a, b, c, d. O‘n ikki soniya.
scenes.say: Put the four sentences in order, from most formal to most colloquial. Twelve seconds.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta gapni eng rasmiysidan eng so‘zlashuvgacha tartiblang. O‘n ikki soniya.

scenes.title: Javob: tartib
board: d → b → c → a
d: website / official message
b: neutral, polite · c: informal · a: very casual
scenes.say_native: To‘g‘ri tartib: d, b, c, a. “Kindly wait while we process your request” sayt yoki rasmiy xabar tili. “Could you wait a moment, please?” neytral, istalgan joyda xavfsiz. “Hang on a minute” norasmiy, hamkasb yoki tanish bilan. “Gimme a sec” esa “give me a second” ning juda erkin talaffuzi, faqat yaqin odamlar uchun, yozuvda esa faqat chatda.
scenes.say: D, B, C, A. Kindly wait is official. Could you wait a moment is neutral. Hang on a minute is informal. And gimme a sec is a very casual way of saying give me a second.
scenes.say_uz: D, B, C, A. Kindly wait rasmiy. Could you wait a moment neytral. Hang on a minute norasmiy. Gimme a sec esa give me a second ning juda erkin shakli.

scenes.title: Ibora fe’l yoki lotincha fe’l
board: investigate ↔ look into · cancel ↔ call off
discover ↔ find out · continue ↔ carry on
tolerate ↔ put up with · reduce ↔ cut down on

examples.t: The police are investigating the incident.
I'll look into it and get back to you.
examples.uz: Buni o‘rganib chiqaman va sizga xabar beraman. (neytral)

scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilidagi registrning asosiy dastagi ikki qatlamli lug‘at. Lotin va fransuz tilidan kelgan fe’llar, masalan “investigate”, “cancel”, “discover”, rasmiyroq. Germancha ildizli ibora fe’llar, masalan “look into”, “call off”, “find out”, kundalikroq. Ma’no deyarli bir xil, faqat ohang boshqa. Bitta matn ichida bir qatlamni izchil ushlab turing.
scenes.say: English has two layers of vocabulary. The Latinate layer, investigate, cancel, discover, sounds formal. The phrasal verb layer, look into, call off, find out, sounds everyday.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida lug‘atning ikki qatlami bor. Lotincha qatlam, investigate, cancel, discover, rasmiy eshitiladi. Ibora fe’llar qatlami, look into, call off, find out, kundalik eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Mashq: kundalik uslubga o‘tkazing
board: 1) We will investigate your complaint.
2) The match has been cancelled.
3) How did you discover the truth?
4) Please continue with your work.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta rasmiy gapdagi lotincha fe’lni ibora fe’l bilan almashtiring va gapni kundalik nutqqa aylantiring. Zamon va nisbatni saqlang: ikkinchi gap majhul nisbatda, demak ibora fe’l ham majhul shaklda bo‘ladi. Har bir gapni ovoz chiqarib ham ayting. O‘n besh soniya.
scenes.say: Make each sentence more everyday by replacing the Latinate verb with a phrasal verb. Fifteen seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Lotincha fe’lni ibora fe’l bilan almashtirib, har bir gapni kundalikroq qiling. O‘n besh soniya.

scenes.title: Javoblar: ibora fe’llar
board: 1) We'll look into your complaint.
2) The match has been called off.
3) How did you find out the truth?
4) Please carry on with your work.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “We’ll look into your complaint”, qisqartma ham registrni pasaytiradi. Ikkinchi: “The match has been called off”, ibora fe’l majhul nisbatda ham bemalol ishlaydi. Uchinchi: “How did you find out the truth?” To‘rtinchi: “Please carry on with your work” yoki “go on with”. E’tibor bering, bu gaplarning hech biri xato emas, ular shunchaki boshqa registrda.
scenes.say: We'll look into your complaint. The match has been called off. How did you find out the truth? Please carry on with your work.
scenes.say_uz: Shikoyatingizni o‘rganib chiqamiz. O‘yin bekor qilindi. Haqiqatni qanday bilib olding? Iltimos, ishingizni davom ettiring.

scenes.title: So‘zlashuv nutqining belgilari
board: Ellipsis: (Do you) want a coffee? · (I) told you so.
Vague language: sort of · and stuff · or something
Tags: It's freezing, isn't it? · Nice, that.

examples.t: It was sort of strange, you know?

examples.uz: Pitsa va shunga o‘xshash narsalar yedik.

scenes.say_native: So‘zlashuvning uchta belgisi. Birinchisi ellipsis, ya’ni so‘zni tushirish: “Want a coffee?”, “Told you so”. O‘zbekchada ham “Choy ichasanmi?” da “sen” tushib qoladi. Ikkinchisi noaniq til: “sort of”, “and stuff”, “or something”. Bu dangasalik emas, tabiiy nutq belgisi. Uchinchisi so‘roq qo‘shimchalari va qisqa izohlar. Bular og‘zaki nutqda yaxshi, lekin rasmiy yozuvda o‘rinsiz.
scenes.say: Real conversation is full of ellipsis, want a coffee?, and vague language, sort of, and stuff, or something. These aren't mistakes; they're features of natural speech. They just don't belong in an essay.
scenes.say_uz: Jonli suhbat ellipsis, ya’ni kofe ichasanmi, va noaniq iboralar bilan to‘la: qandaydir, va hokazo, yoki shunga o‘xshash. Bular xato emas, tabiiy nutq belgilari. Faqat ularning inshoda joyi yo‘q.

scenes.title: Britaniya so‘zlashuv so‘zlari
board: knackered = very tired · skint = no money
gutted = very disappointed · quid = pound(s)
cheers = thanks / bye · mate = friend

examples.t: I'm absolutely knackered after that shift.
examples.uz: O‘sha smenadan keyin butunlay holdan toydim.

scenes.say_native: Britaniyada eshitadigan so‘zlashuv so‘zlari. “Knackered” juda charchagan, “skint” puli yo‘q, “gutted” juda ko‘ngli qolgan, “quid” funt sterling, ko‘plikda ham “quid”: “twenty quid”. “Cheers” ham rahmat, ham xayr ma’nosida. “Mate” do‘st, notanish erkakka ham ishlatiladi. Bularni britaniyalik hamkasbingiz bilan suhbatda eshitasiz, rasmiy xatda esa hech qachon.
scenes.say: I'm knackered means I'm exhausted. I'm skint means I've got no money. She was gutted means she was bitterly disappointed. And twenty quid is twenty pounds; quid doesn't take an s.
scenes.say_uz: I’m knackered — juda charchadim. I’m skint — pulim yo‘q. She was gutted — uning ko‘ngli juda qoldi. Twenty quid esa yigirma funt, quid ga s qo‘shilmaydi.

scenes.title: Amerika so‘zlashuv so‘zlari
board: bucks = dollars · hang out = spend time
awesome = great · y'all = you (plural, Southern US)
I'm good. = No, thank you. (especially AmE)

examples.t: Want some more? — I'm good, thanks.

scenes.say_native: Amerika so‘zlashuvidan ham bir nechta. “Bucks” dollar, “hang out” birga vaqt o‘tkazmoq, “awesome” zo‘r. “Y’all” janubiy shtatlarda “sizlar” degani. Eng ko‘p chalkashtiradigan ibora “I’m good”: taklifga javoban u “yaxshiman” emas, “yo‘q, rahmat, kerak emas” ma’nosini beradi. Bu ibora asosan amerikacha, lekin Britaniyada ham tobora ko‘p eshitiladi.
scenes.say: In American English, ten bucks is ten dollars, and to hang out is to spend time together. And if someone offers you more food and you say I'm good, you mean no, thank you.
scenes.say_uz: Amerika ingliz tilida ten bucks o‘n dollar, hang out esa birga vaqt o‘tkazish. Kimdir yana ovqat taklif qilsa va siz I’m good desangiz, “yo‘q, rahmat” degan bo‘lasiz.

scenes.title: Slengning xavflari
board: ✗ Slang in an exam essay
✗ Dated slang: It's the bee's knees!
✗ Words you can't judge (some are offensive)
✓ Recognise much, use a little
scenes.say_native: Sleng bilan uchta xavf bor. Birinchisi, uni insho yoki ish xatida ishlatish. Ikkinchisi, eskirgan sleng: kitobdagi ba’zi iboralar o‘nlab yil oldin moda bo‘lgan, hozir esa kulgili eshitiladi. Uchinchisi, ma’nosi yoki ohangini to‘liq bilmagan so‘zni ishlatish, ba’zilari haqoratli bo‘lishi mumkin. C2 qoidasi: ko‘p narsani taniyman, ozini ishlataman, faqat ishonchim komil bo‘lganini.
scenes.say: With slang, recognise much and use little. It dates quickly, it varies from place to place, and some words carry a sting you may not be aware of. If you're not sure, don't.
scenes.say_uz: Slengni ko‘p taning, kam ishlating. U tez eskiradi, joydan joyga farq qiladi va ba’zi so‘zlarda siz bilmagan nish bo‘ladi. Ishonchingiz komil bo‘lmasa, ishlatmang.

scenes.title: Mashq: nimani anglatadi?
board: 1) I'm a bit skint this week.
2) She was gutted about the result.
3) Fancy a coffee? — I'm good, cheers.
4) That'll be ten quid, mate.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta so‘zlashuv gapining ma’nosini neytral ingliz tilida yoki o‘zbekcha ayting. Uchinchi gapga ayniqsa e’tibor bering: unda ikkita so‘zlashuv iborasi bor va javob “ha” emasligini tushunish kerak. Hozirgina o‘rgangan Britaniya so‘zlarini eslang. O‘n ikki soniya.
scenes.say: What do these colloquial sentences mean? Say them in neutral English. Twelve seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Bu so‘zlashuv gaplari nimani anglatadi? Ularni neytral ingliz tilida ayting. O‘n ikki soniya.

scenes.title: Javoblar: so‘zlashuv
board: 1) I don't have much money this week.
2) She was very disappointed.
3) No, thank you. (refusing the coffee)
4) That costs ten pounds.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: bu hafta pulim kam. Ikkinchi: natijadan ko‘ngli juda qoldi. Uchinchi: “Fancy a coffee?” — kofe ichasanmi, “I’m good, cheers” — yo‘q, rahmat. Ko‘p o‘quvchi buni “ha” deb tushunadi. To‘rtinchi: o‘n funt bo‘ladi, “mate” bu yerda sotuvchining do‘stona murojaati. Bu so‘zlarni tanish C2 tinglashi uchun zarur.
scenes.say: I don't have much money this week. She was very disappointed. No, thank you. And that costs ten pounds, said in a friendly way.
scenes.say_uz: Bu hafta pulim kam. Uning ko‘ngli juda qoldi. Yo‘q, rahmat. Va bu o‘n funt turadi, do‘stona ohangda aytilgan.

scenes.title: Birinchi tinglash: ikki qo‘ng‘iroq
board: Listening 1
Kamola calls her manager, then her friend
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash. Kamola ishga kechikmoqda. Avval rahbariga, keyin dugonasiga qo‘ng‘iroq qiladi. Bitta odam, bitta tong, lekin ikki xil registr. Uning so‘z tanlovi, gap uzunligi va murojaat shakli qanday o‘zgarishiga e’tibor bering. Ikki qo‘ng‘iroq orasida qisqa pauza bor.
scenes.say: Good morning, Mr Harris. I'm afraid I'm running a little late; there's been an accident on the ring road. I should be with you by half past nine at the latest. Would you like me to send the figures ahead? Thank you, I'll do that straight away. Hey, it's me! Nightmare morning, I'm stuck in traffic. Probably gonna be late for the gym tonight too. Grab us a spot, will you? Cheers!
scenes.say_uz: Xayrli tong, janob Xarris. Afsuski, biroz kechikyapman, halqa yo‘lda avariya bo‘libdi. Ko‘pi bilan to‘qqiz yarimda yetib boraman. Raqamlarni oldindan yuborib qo‘yaymi? Rahmat, hoziroq yuboraman. Salom, bu men! Dahshatli tong, tirbandlikda qolib ketdim. Kechqurun sport zalga ham kechikadiganga o‘xshayman. Menga joy egallab tur, xo‘pmi? Rahmat!

scenes.title: Birinchi tinglash savollari
board: 1) Why is Kamola late?
2) Find two features of formal register in call 1.
3) Find two colloquial features in call 2.
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: Kamola nega kechikmoqda. Ikkinchi: birinchi qo‘ng‘iroqdan rasmiy registrning ikkita belgisini toping. Uchinchi: ikkinchi qo‘ng‘iroqdan so‘zlashuvning ikkita belgisini toping. Ikkinchi va uchinchi savollarda bittadan ko‘p to‘g‘ri javob bor. O‘n besh soniya.
scenes.say: Three questions about Kamola's two calls. Fifteen seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Kamolaning ikki qo‘ng‘irog‘i haqida uchta savol. O‘n besh soniya.

scenes.title: Javoblar: birinchi tinglash
board: 1) An accident on the ring road
2) Mr Harris · I'm afraid · at the latest · Would you like me to…?
3) Hey, it's me · Nightmare morning (ellipsis) · gonna · Grab us a spot, will you? · Cheers
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: halqa yo‘ldagi avariya. Ikkinchi: rasmiy belgilar — “Mr Harris” murojaati, yumshatuvchi “I’m afraid”, “at the latest”, taklif shakli “Would you like me to…?”. Uchinchi: so‘zlashuv belgilari — “Hey, it’s me”, to‘liq bo‘lmagan gap “Nightmare morning”, “gonna”, so‘roq qo‘shimchasi bilan buyruq “Grab us a spot, will you?”. Britaniya so‘zlashuvida “us” ba’zan “me” o‘rnida keladi.
scenes.say: An accident on the ring road. In the first call: Mr Harris, I'm afraid, would you like me to. In the second: hey, it's me, nightmare morning, gonna, grab us a spot, will you, and cheers.
scenes.say_uz: Halqa yo‘ldagi avariya. Birinchi qo‘ng‘iroqda: Mr Harris, I’m afraid, would you like me to. Ikkinchisida: hey, it’s me, nightmare morning, gonna, grab us a spot, will you va cheers.

scenes.title: Registrni qachon almashtirish kerak
board: Start neutral, then follow the other person
Signals: first names, contractions, jokes
Move down slowly; moving back up is awkward
scenes.say_native: Amaliy qoida: yangi vaziyatda neytral registrdan boshlang va suhbatdoshga ergashing. Agar u “Please, call me Tom” desa, qisqartmalar va hazil ishlatsa, siz ham bir pog‘ona pastga tushishingiz mumkin. Lekin asta-sekin tushing: haddan ortiq erkinlikdan keyin rasmiy uslubga qaytish noqulay. O‘zbek madaniyatidagi “sen” ga o‘tishga ruxsat so‘rash kabi, bu ham ehtiyotkorlik talab qiladi.
scenes.say: Start neutral and follow the other person's lead. If they switch to first names, contractions and jokes, you can relax too. But move down gradually: it's much harder to climb back up.
scenes.say_uz: Neytral boshlang va suhbatdoshga ergashing. U ismga, qisqartmalarga va hazilga o‘tsa, siz ham bo‘shashishingiz mumkin. Lekin asta tushing: qaytib ko‘tarilish ancha qiyin.

scenes.title: Elektron xatdagi registr
board: Dear Sir or Madam, … Yours faithfully, (BrE)
Dear Ms Rahimova, … Yours sincerely, / Kind regards,
Hi Anna, … Best, / Thanks,
Hey! … See you!
scenes.say_native: Xatda registr boshlanish va yakunlanishdan ko‘rinadi. Ismni bilmasangiz: “Dear Sir or Madam” va Britaniyada “Yours faithfully”. Ismni bilsangiz: “Dear Ms Rahimova” va “Yours sincerely” yoki ishda ko‘p ishlatiladigan “Kind regards”. Amerikada ikkala holatda ham ko‘pincha “Sincerely” yoziladi. Hamkasbga “Hi Anna” va “Best”, do‘stga “Hey”.
scenes.say: If you don't know the name, it's Dear Sir or Madam and, in British English, Yours faithfully. If you do, Dear Ms Rahimova and Yours sincerely, or Kind regards. Americans tend to use Sincerely for both.
scenes.say_uz: Ismni bilmasangiz, Dear Sir or Madam va Britaniyada Yours faithfully. Bilsangiz, Dear Ms Rahimova va Yours sincerely yoki Kind regards. Amerikaliklar ikkalasida ham ko‘pincha Sincerely yozadi.

scenes.title: O‘qituvchiga yozilgan xat
board: ✗ hey prof!! need the slides asap thx
✗ No greeting, no name, no 'please'
✓ Dear Professor Karimov, …
scenes.say_native: Talabalar ko‘p qiladigan xato: professorga chatdagidek yozish. “Hey prof!! need the slides asap thx” xatida murojaat yo‘q, ism yo‘q, “please” yo‘q, “asap” esa talab ohangini beradi. Professor sizga yordam berishi mumkin, lekin taassurot yomon qoladi. Rasmiy xat qisqa bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin to‘liq bo‘lishi shart.
scenes.say: Hey prof, need the slides asap, thanks. Short, yes, but it sounds like a demand sent to a friend. A formal email can be brief, but it still needs a greeting, a polite request and a sign-off.
scenes.say_uz: Hey prof, slaydlar tezda kerak, rahmat. Qisqa, ha, lekin do‘stga yuborilgan talabga o‘xshaydi. Rasmiy xat qisqa bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin unda murojaat, muloyim so‘rov va yakun bo‘lishi kerak.

scenes.title: Mashq: xatni qayta yozing
board: hey prof!! need the slides from tuesday asap thx
→ Rewrite it for Professor Karimov.
Greeting · polite request · thanks · sign-off
scenes.say_native: Shu xatni professor Karimovga mos registrda qayta yozing. To‘rt qism bo‘lsin: murojaat, muloyim so‘rov, minnatdorchilik va yakun. “I was wondering if” kabi yumshatuvchi tuzilmani ishlatib ko‘ring. Yigirma soniya kamlik qilsa, to‘xtatib, bemalol yozing.
scenes.say: Rewrite the message for Professor Karimov: greeting, polite request, thanks and sign-off. Twenty seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Xatni professor Karimov uchun qayta yozing: murojaat, muloyim so‘rov, minnatdorchilik va yakun. Yigirma soniya.

scenes.title: Namuna xat
board: Dear Professor Karimov,
I was wondering whether you might be able to share the slides from Tuesday's lecture.
Many thanks in advance. Kind regards, Nodira Aliyeva
scenes.say_native: Namunaga qarang. Murojaat to‘liq unvon bilan. So‘rov “I was wondering whether you might be able to” bilan yumshatilgan, “asap” olib tashlangan. Qaysi slaydlar kerakligi aniq aytilgan: seshanbadagi ma’ruza. Oxirida minnatdorchilik, yakun va to‘liq ism. Hammasi uch qator, lekin taassurot butunlay boshqa.
scenes.say: Dear Professor Karimov, I was wondering whether you might be able to share the slides from Tuesday's lecture. Many thanks in advance. Kind regards, Nodira Aliyeva.
scenes.say_uz: Hurmatli professor Karimov, seshanbadagi ma’ruza slaydlarini ulasha olmaysizmikan deb so‘ramoqchi edim. Oldindan katta rahmat. Hurmat bilan, Nodira Aliyeva.

scenes.title: Yozma va og‘zaki nutq farqi
board: Writing: complete sentences · nominalisation · explicit links
Speech: fragments · fillers · discourse markers (So, Right, Anyway)
Speech: heads and tails — That film, it was brilliant. · He's clever, your brother.
scenes.say_native: Registr faqat rasmiylik emas, kanal ham. Yozma tilda gaplar to‘liq, bog‘lovchilar aniq, otlashtirish ko‘p. Og‘zaki nutqda esa to‘liq bo‘lmagan gaplar, “so”, “right”, “anyway” kabi nutq belgilari va mavzuni oldinga yoki oxirga chiqarish uchraydi: “That film, it was brilliant”, “He’s clever, your brother”. O‘zbekchada ham “Akang-chi, u aqlli” deymiz. Bular og‘zaki nutqda to‘g‘ri, yozuvda emas.
scenes.say: Speech and writing follow different rules. In conversation we say things like that film, it was brilliant, or he's clever, your brother. In writing, those would look like errors.
scenes.say_uz: Og‘zaki va yozma nutqning qoidalari boshqa. Suhbatda “o‘sha film, u zo‘r edi” yoki “aqlli-da, akang” deymiz. Yozuvda esa bular xatoga o‘xshaydi.

scenes.title: Bitta mazmun, ikki kanal
board: Spoken: So basically, loads of people are moving to the city, right? And there just aren't enough flats.
Written: Rapid migration to the city has led to a severe housing shortage.
scenes.say_native: Bitta mazmunni ikki kanalda solishtiring. Og‘zaki variantda “so basically”, “loads of”, “right?” va ikki gapga bo‘lingan fikr bor. Yozma variantda esa hammasi bitta gapda: “rapid migration” otlashtirish, “has led to” sabab-natija bog‘lovchisi, “severe housing shortage” zich ot birikmasi. Og‘zaki variant 17 so‘z, yozma gap esa atigi 12 so‘z.
scenes.say: So basically, loads of people are moving to the city, right? And there just aren't enough flats. In writing, that becomes: rapid migration to the city has led to a severe housing shortage.
scenes.say_uz: Xullas, juda ko‘p odam shaharga ko‘chib kelyapti, to‘g‘rimi? Kvartiralar esa yetishmaydi. Yozuvda bu shunday bo‘ladi: shaharga tez ko‘chish jiddiy uy-joy tanqisligiga olib keldi.

scenes.title: Mashq: og‘zakidan yozmaga
board: Spoken: Prices are going up like crazy, and, like, young people just can't afford to buy anything.
→ Write one formal sentence.
scenes.say_native: Og‘zaki gapni bitta rasmiy yozma gapga aylantiring. “Like crazy”, “like” va “just” ni olib tashlang, “going up” o‘rniga rasmiyroq fe’l yoki otlashtirish ishlating, ikkita fikrni sabab-natija bilan bog‘lang. Gap uzunligi o‘n besh so‘zdan oshmasin. Yigirma soniya.
scenes.say: Turn the spoken sentence into one formal written sentence. Twenty seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Og‘zaki gapni bitta rasmiy yozma gapga aylantiring. Yigirma soniya.

scenes.title: Namuna javob: yozma gap
board: The sharp rise in prices has left many young people unable to afford property.
going up like crazy → the sharp rise
can't afford to buy anything → unable to afford property
scenes.say_native: Namuna: “The sharp rise in prices has left many young people unable to afford property”. “Going up like crazy” otlashtirilib “the sharp rise” bo‘ldi, ikki fikr “has left … unable to” orqali bog‘landi, “anything” esa aniqroq “property” bilan almashtirildi. Sizning variantingizda “Rising prices mean that…” bo‘lsa ham to‘g‘ri, muhimi slengsiz, aniq va bitta mantiqiy gap.
scenes.say: The sharp rise in prices has left many young people unable to afford property. One sentence, no fillers, and a clear cause and effect.
scenes.say_uz: Narxlarning keskin oshishi ko‘plab yoshlarni uy-joy sotib olish imkoniyatidan mahrum qildi. Bitta gap, ortiqcha so‘zsiz va aniq sabab-natija bilan.

scenes.title: Ikkinchi tinglash: e’lon va qayta hikoya
board: Listening 2
A station announcement, then a friend retells it
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Avval vokzaldagi rasmiy e’lonni, keyin do‘stning uni sherigiga qayta aytib berishini eshitasiz. Rasmiy iboralar so‘zlashuvda qanday “tarjima” qilinishiga e’tibor bering. Vaqt va platforma raqamini ham yozib oling. E’londa yigirma to‘rt soatlik vaqt ishlatiladi.
scenes.say: Ladies and gentlemen, we regret to announce that the eighteen forty-five service to Manchester has been cancelled due to a signalling fault. Passengers are advised to take the nineteen ten service, which will depart from platform four. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause. Friend: Bad news, the quarter to seven's been cancelled. Something to do with the signals. We'll have to get the ten past, platform four. Typical!
scenes.say_uz: Hurmatli yo‘lovchilar, afsus bilan ma’lum qilamizki, Manchesterga soat 18:45 dagi reys signal tizimidagi nosozlik tufayli bekor qilindi. Yo‘lovchilarga to‘rtinchi platformadan jo‘naydigan 19:10 reysidan foydalanish tavsiya etiladi. Noqulaylik uchun uzr so‘raymiz. Do‘st: Yomon xabar, yettiga chorakam poyezd bekor bo‘libdi. Signallar bilan bog‘liq nimadir. O‘n daqiqasi o‘tganiga, to‘rtinchi platformaga borishimiz kerak. Har doimgidek!

scenes.title: Ikkinchi tinglash savollari
board: 1) Why was the train cancelled?
2) Which train should passengers take, and from where?
3) What did the friend say instead of: a) we regret to announce  b) due to a signalling fault  c) take the 19:10 service?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: poyezd nega bekor qilindi. Ikkinchi: yo‘lovchilar qaysi poyezdga va qaysi platformadan chiqishi kerak. Uchinchi: do‘st uchta rasmiy ibora o‘rniga nima dedi. Uchinchi savol registr almashishining aniq namunasi, shuning uchun iboralarni aynan eslang. O‘n besh soniya.
scenes.say: Three questions about the announcement and the friend's version. Fifteen seconds.
scenes.say_uz: E’lon va do‘stning varianti haqida uchta savol. O‘n besh soniya.

scenes.title: Javoblar: ikkinchi tinglash
board: 1) A signalling fault
2) The 19:10, from platform four
3) a) Bad news  b) Something to do with the signals  c) We'll have to get the ten past
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: signal tizimidagi nosozlik. Ikkinchi: soat 19:10 dagi poyezd, to‘rtinchi platformadan. Uchinchi: “we regret to announce” o‘rniga “bad news”, “due to a signalling fault” o‘rniga noaniq “something to do with the signals”, “take the 19:10 service” o‘rniga “get the ten past”. Do‘st 24 soatlik vaqtni ham “quarter to seven”, “ten past” ga aylantirdi, bu ham so‘zlashuv belgisi.
scenes.say: A signalling fault. The nineteen ten, from platform four. And the friend said bad news, something to do with the signals, and we'll have to get the ten past.
scenes.say_uz: Signal nosozligi. 19:10 dagi poyezd, to‘rtinchi platformadan. Do‘st esa bad news, something to do with the signals va we’ll have to get the ten past dedi.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: erkin nutqdagi qisqarishlar
board: going to → gonna · want to → wanna · got to → gotta
don't know → dunno · do you → d'you
✗ I'm gonna London.  ✓ I'm going to London.
scenes.say_native: Erkin nutqda so‘zlar qo‘shilib qisqaradi: “going to” — “gonna”, “want to” — “wanna”, “got to” — “gotta”, “don’t know” — “dunno”. Ularni tushunish shart, ishlatish esa ixtiyoriy. Bitta muhim qoida: “gonna” faqat “going to” dan keyin fe’l kelganda ishlaydi. “I’m gonna call you” to‘g‘ri, lekin “I’m gonna London” xato, chunki bu yerda “going” harakat fe’li.
scenes.say: In relaxed speech, going to becomes gonna, but only before a verb. I'm gonna call you is fine. I'm gonna London is wrong, because there going is a real verb of movement.
scenes.say_uz: Erkin nutqda going to gonna ga aylanadi, lekin faqat fe’ldan oldin. I’m gonna call you to‘g‘ri. I’m gonna London esa xato, chunki u yerda going haqiqiy harakat fe’li.

scenes.title: Mashq: to‘liq shaklda yozing
board: 1) Whatcha doing?
2) I dunno.
3) Gotta go!
4) D'you wanna grab a bite?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta so‘zlashuv iborasini to‘liq, standart shaklda yozing va ma’nosini ayting. To‘rtinchisida qisqarishdan tashqari bitta so‘zlashuv iborasi ham bor, uni neytral ifoda bilan almashtiring. Qisqartmalarda apostrofni to‘g‘ri joyga qo‘ying. O‘n ikki soniya.
scenes.say: Write each phrase out in full, standard English. Twelve seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir iborani to‘liq, standart ingliz tilida yozing. O‘n ikki soniya.

scenes.title: Javoblar: to‘liq shakllar
board: 1) What are you doing?
2) I don't know.
3) I've got to go!
4) Do you want to get something to eat?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “What are you doing?” Ikkinchi: “I don’t know”. Uchinchi: “I’ve got to go”, ya’ni ketishim kerak, bu yerda “I’ve” ham tushib qolgan. To‘rtinchi: “Do you want to get something to eat?”, chunki “grab a bite” — tez biror narsa yeb olmoq. Bu shakllarni chat va sms da ko‘rasiz, lekin rasmiy xatda yozmang.
scenes.say: What are you doing? I don't know. I've got to go. Do you want to get something to eat? You'll see the short forms in text messages, but never in formal writing.
scenes.say_uz: Nima qilyapsan? Bilmayman. Ketishim kerak. Biror narsa yeb olishni xohlaysanmi? Qisqa shakllarni xabarlarda ko‘rasiz, lekin rasmiy yozuvda hech qachon.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: uch registr
board: Message: You can't come to tomorrow's meeting.
Write it in 3 registers:
1 formal (to a client)  2 neutral (to a colleague)  3 colloquial (to a friend)
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy topshiriq. Ertangi yig‘ilishga kela olmaysiz. Shu xabarni uch registrda yozing: mijozga rasmiy, hamkasbga neytral va do‘stga so‘zlashuv uslubida. Har birida bugungi belgilardan foydalaning: rasmiyda lotincha so‘z va yumshatish, neytralda qisqartma, so‘zlashuvda ellipsis. Yigirma soniya kamlik qilsa, to‘xtatib yozing.
scenes.say: You can't come to tomorrow's meeting. Write that message three times: to a client, to a colleague and to a friend.
scenes.say_uz: Ertangi yig‘ilishga kela olmaysiz. Shu xabarni uch marta yozing: mijozga, hamkasbga va do‘stga.

scenes.title: Namuna: uch registr
board: Formal: I regret that I will be unable to attend tomorrow's meeting owing to a prior commitment.
Neutral: I'm sorry, but I won't be able to make tomorrow's meeting.
Colloquial: Can't make it tomorrow, sorry!
scenes.say_native: Namunalarni solishtiring. Rasmiy variantda “regret”, “unable to attend”, “owing to a prior commitment”, ya’ni sabab umumiy va muloyim berilgan. Neytralda “I’m sorry, but” va “make the meeting”, ya’ni ulgurmoq ma’nosidagi ibora. So‘zlashuvda esa ega tushib qolgan: “Can’t make it tomorrow, sorry!”. Uchala gap to‘g‘ri, faqat har biri o‘z joyida.
scenes.say: I regret that I will be unable to attend tomorrow's meeting owing to a prior commitment. I'm sorry, but I won't be able to make tomorrow's meeting. Can't make it tomorrow, sorry!
scenes.say_uz: Afsuski, oldindan rejalashtirilgan ish sababli ertangi yig‘ilishda qatnasha olmayman. Kechirasiz, ertangi yig‘ilishga kela olmayman. Ertaga ulgurmayman, kechir!

scenes.title: Xulosa
board: Spectrum: formal → neutral → informal → colloquial → slang
Tools: Latinate vs phrasal · contractions · ellipsis · softeners
Switch: start neutral, follow the other person
Writing ≠ speech
scenes.say_native: Bugungi darsni jamlaylik. Registr besh pog‘onali shkala, uni so‘z qatlami, grammatika, qisqartmalar va yumshatuvchi iboralar belgilaydi. Slengni ko‘p taniymiz, kam ishlatamiz. Yangi vaziyatda neytraldan boshlab, suhbatdoshga ergashamiz. Yozma va og‘zaki nutqning qoidalari esa alohida. C2 egasi bu pog‘onalar orasida erkin harakatlanadi.
scenes.say: A C2 speaker moves up and down the register ladder without effort: formal with a client, neutral with a colleague, relaxed with a friend, and always appropriate.
scenes.say_uz: C2 egasi registr zinapoyasida bemalol yuqoriga va pastga harakatlanadi: mijoz bilan rasmiy, hamkasb bilan neytral, do‘st bilan erkin va har doim o‘rinli.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: rewrite one message in 3 registers
Success: each version fits its reader; at least 2 register markers in each
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘zingiz yaqinda yozgan bitta haqiqiy xabarni oling va uni uch registrda qayta yozing: rasmiy, neytral va so‘zlashuv. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: har bir variant o‘z o‘quvchisiga mos va unda kamida ikkita registr belgisi bor, masalan lotincha fe’l, qisqartma yoki ellipsis. Keyingi darsda kesatiq, yumor va kinoyani o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Take one real message you've written recently and rewrite it in three registers. Next time, we look at sarcasm, humour and irony.
scenes.say_uz: Yaqinda yozgan bitta haqiqiy xabaringizni olib, uni uch registrda qayta yozing. Keyingi safar kesatiq, yumor va kinoyani ko‘rib chiqamiz.

homework_uz: Yaqinda yozgan bitta haqiqiy xabaringizni (masalan, kechikish, uchrashuvni ko‘chirish yoki iltimos) uch registrda qayta yozing: rasmiy (mijoz yoki rahbarga), neytral (hamkasbga) va so‘zlashuv (do‘stga). Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: har bir variant o‘z o‘quvchisiga mos va unda kamida ikkita registr belgisi bor (lotincha fe’l yoki ibora fe’l, qisqartma, ellipsis, yumshatuvchi ibora).

quiz.q: Which sentence is the most formal?
options: Could you wait a moment, please?
Kindly wait while we process your request.
quiz.why_uz: Kindly va process your request — rasmiy, rasmiy xabarlar tili.

quiz.q: Which is the everyday phrasal-verb equivalent of 'investigate'?
quiz.why_uz: Investigate ↔ look into: o‘rganib chiqmoq, tekshirmoq.
Call off — bekor qilmoq; majhul nisbatda: has been called off.
Skint — puli yo‘q. Knackered — charchagan, gutted — ko‘ngli qolgan.

quiz.q: Someone offers you more cake and you reply 'I'm good, thanks.' You mean…
quiz.why_uz: Taklifga javoban I’m good — yo‘q, rahmat, kerak emas.

quiz.q: Which opening and closing match in a formal British letter to an unknown person?
options: Dear Sir or Madam … Yours faithfully
quiz.why_uz: Ism noma’lum bo‘lsa: Dear Sir or Madam va Yours faithfully (BrE).
Gonna faqat going to + fe’l o‘rnida ishlatiladi. London oldida going harakat fe’li: I’m going to London.

quiz.q: Which feature is typical of speech but NOT of formal writing?
quiz.why_uz: So‘zni tushirib qoldirish (ellipsis) og‘zaki nutq belgisi.

quiz.q: Which is the best formal version of 'Can't make it tomorrow, sorry!'?
options: I regret that I will be unable to attend tomorrow.
quiz.why_uz: Regret va unable to attend — rasmiy registr belgilari.

quiz.q: What is the safest register to start with in a new professional situation?
quiz.why_uz: Neytral registrdan boshlab, suhbatdoshga ergashish eng xavfsiz yo‘l.
